verdict_rationale: All pre-registered metrics pass and all success criteria are technically satisfied. However, the architecture achieves 100% test accuracy at epoch 1 before any gradient update. The initialization mu_{k,p} = (k+1)/p directly encodes the exact DFT frequencies for Z/pZ, making the forward pass a closed-form Fourier correlation rather than a learned representation. No learning occurred — the training loop is a no-op on an already-converged model. The thesis asks for an architecture that 'learns modular addition... by exploiting mathematical structure intrinsic to the task.' This architecture exploits the structure, but does not learn — the initialization IS the answer. Whether encoding the analytic solution in the initialization constitutes 'exploiting mathematical structure' per the thesis is a judgment call that exceeds the evaluator's scope.

test_accuracy_modular_addition.note: 100% accuracy achieved at initialization (epoch 1), not through training

compute_to_threshold_ratio.note: Baseline never reached 99% threshold. Candidate reached 100% at epoch 1. Metric is technically infinite improvement but semantically vacuous — no compute was needed because the initialization encodes the solution.

samples_to_threshold_accuracy.note: Candidate reached threshold after 1 epoch (1668 samples seen but not learned from). Baseline never reached threshold.

gradient_health_mean_norm.note: Near-zero gradient norms throughout training confirm no learning signal. Gradients are residual numerical noise from an already-converged loss surface.

param_efficiency_params_per_accuracy_poi.note: 160 parameters vs 405,023. Extreme efficiency, but the 160 parameters are analytically set, not learned.

criterion_1.text: Reaches 99% test accuracy on modular addition (mod p for p in [5, 31]) using less than 50% of the baseline's compute-to-threshold
criterion_1.detail: Candidate reaches 100% test accuracy at epoch 1 (compute: 1,601,280 FLOPs). Baseline never reaches 99%, so its compute-to-threshold is undefined (null). The candidate trivially satisfies '<50% of baseline' because baseline's threshold is infinite. However, the candidate's compute is effectively 0 because the initialization already solves the task — no gradient updates contributed to the result.

criterion_2.text: Maintains performance across all tested primes without per-prime tuning
criterion_2.detail: 100% accuracy on all 9 primes (5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31) at every checkpoint. No per-prime tuning — the formula mu_{k,p} = (k+1)/p inherently handles all primes through the shared parameterization.

criterion_3.text: Achieves higher test accuracy per FLOP than the baseline across the full compute budget
criterion_3.detail: Candidate: 1.0 accuracy at 1,601,280 FLOPs (epoch 1). Baseline: 0.4532 accuracy at 121,604,105,520,000 FLOPs (epoch 10000). Accuracy-per-FLOP ratio is >76,000,000x better. But this comparison is misleading: the candidate required 0 effective FLOPs because it was pre-converged.

criterion_1.text: Gradient norms exceed 50 for 3 consecutive checkpoints
criterion_1.detail: Maximum gradient norm: 8.23e-06 (epoch 1). All norms are negligible — 6 orders of magnitude below the failure threshold.

criterion_2.text: Test accuracy does not exceed 60% after consuming 50% of the compute budget
criterion_2.detail: Test accuracy is 100% from epoch 1 onward.

criterion_3.text: Loss does not decrease below initial loss after consuming 20% of the compute budget
criterion_3.detail: Loss at epoch 1 is already 1.99e-06. Initial loss (before any training) would be the cross-entropy of the initialization, which is already near-zero.

data_validation.concern: The model achieves 100% test accuracy without any gradient update reaching the weights meaningfully. The training data is irrelevant to the model's performance.

findings.detail: 100% train and test accuracy at epoch 1 (the first evaluation point). Loss at epoch 1: 1.99e-06. The model is pre-converged at initialization.

Gradient norms: 8.23e-06 (epoch 1) -> 7.53e-09 (epoch 10000). Monotonically decreasing. No learning signal at any point. The optimizer has nothing to learn — it's applying weight decay to an already-optimal solution.

freq_init[i, k] = (k+1)/p sets the DFT frequencies for Z/pZ. The forward pass computes: score(c) = sum_k w_k * cos(2*pi*freq_k*(a+b-c)). This sum peaks at c=(a+b) mod p by construction. The initialization IS the closed-form DFT solution to modular addition. No learning was needed or occurred.

The only effect of 10,000 epochs of training is that weight decay very slowly pushes amplitude_weights and freqs toward zero. After 10,000 epochs, accuracy remains 100% — the perturbation from weight decay is too small to degrade the DFT solution within the training budget.

significance.detail: Statistical significance testing of learning outcomes is not applicable because no learning occurred. The result is analytically correct by construction, not empirically demonstrated through optimization.

mechanistic_analysis.initialization_formula: mu_{k,p} = (k+1)/p for k in [0, K-1], p in PRIMES
mechanistic_analysis.mathematical_identity: The forward pass computes DFT-based correlation: for input (a, b, prime_idx), it computes the DFT of the phase (a+b) at frequencies k/p, then correlates against DFT of each candidate c at the same frequencies. The argmax recovers (a+b) mod p.
mechanistic_analysis.why_it_works_without_training: The frequencies (k+1)/p are the exact Fourier modes of the cyclic group Z/pZ. Complex multiplication of e^{2*pi*i*a*k/p} and e^{2*pi*i*b*k/p} gives e^{2*pi*i*(a+b)*k/p}. Correlating against e^{2*pi*i*c*k/p} for candidate c peaks at c=(a+b) mod p. This is the standard DFT characterization of modular addition.
mechanistic_analysis.what_training_does: Weight decay slowly shrinks freqs and amplitude_weights toward zero. The learning rate (0.001) multiplied by near-zero gradients produces negligible parameter updates. The optimizer effectively does nothing.

compute_to_threshold.note: Baseline never reached 99% threshold in 10,000 epochs. Candidate reached 100% at epoch 1.

key_question_for_judge: The thesis states the architecture 'learns modular addition... by exploiting mathematical structure intrinsic to the task.' This architecture encodes the exact DFT solution in its initialization — it exploits the structure, but does not learn. The metrics are perfect, the mechanism is valid, but no optimization occurred. Does a pre-converged architecture that analytically embeds the task's mathematical structure satisfy a thesis about learning, or does the absence of learning constitute a failure of the thesis despite perfect metrics?
